references.text: Jesus says something very similar earlier in Luke: "If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me." This is a parallel statement about bearing the cross as a condition for being a disciple ([ref:Luk 9:23|Luke 9:23]).

In Matthew, Jesus uses the same image: "Whoever does not take their cross and follow after me is not worthy of me." Bearing the cross is inseparably linked to following Jesus ([ref:Matt 10:38|Matthew 10:38]).

Here too, Jesus speaks of self-denial and bearing the cross as conditions for discipleship: "If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me" ([ref:Matt 16:24|Matthew 16:24]).

Mark's parallel to the statement on bearing the cross: Jesus called the crowd and his disciples to him and said that whoever wants to follow him must deny themselves and take up their cross ([ref:Mark 8:34|Mark 8:34]).

The immediately preceding verse sets the context: one must "hate" their family and even their own life in order to be Jesus' disciple. Verse 27 continues this with the requirement of bearing the cross ([ref:Luk 14:26|Luke 14:26]).

The passage concludes with a summary of the cost of discipleship: "In the same way, none of you can be my disciple unless they give up everything they own." Bearing the cross and giving up all things go together ([ref:Luk 14:33|Luke 14:33]).

Paul expresses the reality of bearing the cross in his own life: "I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me." This is a practical outworking of what it means to bear one's cross and follow Jesus ([ref:Gal 2:20|Galatians 2:20]).

Paul does not want to boast about anything except the cross of Jesus Christ, "by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world." The cross is central in the life of a disciple ([ref:Gal 6:14|Galatians 6:14]).
Paul warns tearfully against those who live as "enemies of the cross of Christ." Refusing to bear the cross is the opposite of true discipleship ([ref:Fil 3:18|Philippians 3:18]).

Paul writes that we are God's heirs and co-heirs with Christ, "provided we suffer with him in order that we may also be glorified with him." Suffering with Christ – bearing the cross – is the path to glory ([ref:Rom 8:17|Romans 8:17]).
"All who desire to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted." Bearing the cross involves a willingness to suffer for Christ's sake ([ref:2 Tim 3:12|2 Timothy 3:12]).
